subject: Interim advisory + postmortem follow-up: elevated 5xx/timeouts for rw-medium-2
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Thompson <sarah.thompson@velocity.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-28T09:12:00Z
Subject: Interim advisory: elevated 5xx/timeouts affecting rw-medium-2

Hi Sarah —

Quick heads-up: between ~08:55–09:05 UTC we observed a spike in 5xx and timeout errors for the model variant rw-medium-2 serving in us-east1 which affected a subset of customer requests. Our telemetry shows increased request latency followed by downstream worker restarts that led to transient 5xx responses.

What we did immediately:
- Enabled an automatic fallback to the compatible rw-medium-2-quant fallback pool for affected routes to reduce error rates.
- Increased instance restart threshold to avoid oscillation while we investigate.
- Rolled a targeted routing rule to move affected requests to healthy nodes.

Impact: you may have seen ~10–20% request failures on your /v1/infer/document-summarize route between 08:55–09:10 UTC. We estimate that the majority of requests succeeded after fallback, but some timeouts persisted.

Next steps: Jonas and engineering are doing a root-cause triage now; we'll follow up with a technical update within 2 hours and a full postmortem in ~3 business days. If you can share any request IDs or traces from your side (sample IDs are fine), that will help accelerate debugging.

Apologies for the interruption — we know this impacts your users. I'll keep you updated.

— Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
(Attachment: logs_excerpt_20260228.txt, text/plain)

From: Sarah Thompson <sarah.thompson@velocity.ai>

Subject: Re: Interim advisory: elevated 5xx/timeouts affecting rw-medium-2

Hi Marcus —

Thanks for the quick note. We did see user-facing errors starting ~08:58 UTC and had to enable client-side retries. The errors correlate with document-summarize requests for large inputs (avg token length ~4k). I can pull and share a few request IDs (attaching two).

Can you confirm whether retries will be safe (idempotency), and whether this counts toward our SLA? We have an all-hands in 30 minutes and will need an ETA for full recovery.

— Sarah
Head of SRE, Velocity AI
sarah.thompson@velocity.ai
(Attachment: velocity_reqids_02-28.csv, text/csv)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Thompson <sarah.thompson@velocity.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-28T09:38:00Z
Subject: Re: Interim advisory: elevated 5xx/timeouts affecting rw-medium-2

Hi Sarah —

Appreciate the IDs, that helped. Quick technical summary from triage so far:
- Root cause (interim): a regression in the kernel-selection code when handling high variance in sequence-length distributions. For long sequences we triggered a slow execution path that increased memory pressure; a small percentage of workers hit an OOM/restart, producing 5xx responses.
- Why fallback didn't fully eliminate timeouts: fallback routing introduced a mix of quantized variants that had different performance characteristics under long sequences; combined with queueing on healthy nodes this produced some timeouts while draining.

Mitigations applied:
1) Stopped sending new traffic to the small set of degraded workers (routing rule in place).
2) Increased scaling headroom for rw-medium-2 pools in us-east1 for the next 2 hours.
3) Pushed a hotfix to kernel-selection heuristics to avoid the pathological branch for sequences > 2k tokens.

Preliminary impact: error rate dropped from ~18% to ~1.8% over the 20-minute window after the fixes. We will continue monitoring; I expect error rates to remain low while we validate.

On retries: safe for idempotent requests if you include the same dedupe/request-id header; for non-idempotent operations we recommend application-level safeguards.

I'll follow up with a short postmortem once we've verified stability.

— Jonas Weber
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.ai

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-28T10:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Interim advisory: elevated 5xx/timeouts affecting rw-medium-2 (internal)

Internal note — for Marcus/Jo: Velocity will likely ask about SLA credit given the visible user impact. Recommend we: 
- Offer a one-time service credit for 10% of impacted monthly usage for the affected window (subject to finance sign-off).
- Include mitigation timeline and the postmortem PDF with proposed long-term fixes (kernel heuristics + better fallback flow).
- Offer a second call with their SREs to review tail latency patterns and advise on request-size limits or early truncation strategies.

If you're OK I can draft the postmortem and the credit note for your review.

— Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Thompson <sarah.thompson@velocity.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-03-03T15:20:00Z
Subject: Postmortem & resolution: rw-medium-2 elevated 5xx/timeouts (Feb 28)

Hi Sarah —

Apologies again for the disruption on Feb 28. Attached is the postmortem and a summary of next steps. TL;DR:
- Incident window: 2026-02-28 08:55–09:10 UTC (primary impact) with residual elevated latency through 09:40 UTC while pools drained.
- Root cause: kernel-selection heuristic regression for high-variance sequence lengths that pushed a small subset of workers into a slow execution path and restarts.
- Resolution: hotfix to heuristic rolled at 09:02 UTC; targeted routing and scaling prevented further restarts. Error rate returned to baseline (~0.1%) by 09:30 UTC.

Actions we completed:
- Hotfix deployed and validated (Jonas).
- Additional unit tests for sequence-length routing added to CI.
- Fallback flow rework scheduled for Q2 to ensure quantized variant latency parity under long inputs.
- Offering Velocity a one-time credit equivalent to 10% of impacted usage in the Feb billing cycle; Marissa will send formal credit note and finance ticket.

Attachments: incident_postmortem_rw-medium-2_20260303.pdf (contains timeline, logs excerpt, and remediation plan).

Proposed next steps:
1) Marissa to send formal credit and coordinate with finance.
2) Offer a technical deep-dive call to Velocity SREs next week to review tail-latency and input-shaping strategies.
3) We'll provide a diagnostic dashboard view for your account surface showing sequence-length distributions and per-route latencies.

Please let me know if you'd like us to schedule the deep-dive — Jonas and I can join.

Thanks for your patience.

— Marcus Lin
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
(Attachment: incident_postmortem_rw-medium-2_20260303.pdf, application/pdf)
